name: Harhur
overview: Harhur was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role is specifically noted in the book of Ezra, indicating his participation in the religious duties associated with the temple during the post-exilic period. No additional personal details or notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Harhur may mean 'fever,' 'raven,' or 'one born during mother’s fever,' reflecting possible Hebrew roots. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 2:51 and was not given directly by God, but it carries cultural significance tied to its possible meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Harhur as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Harhur's significance lies in his role as a temple servant during the restoration period after the Babylonian exile. His inclusion in the list of returnees in Ezra 2:51 highlights the continuity of Levitical service and the reestablishment of proper worship under God's covenant. Though not prominent in narrative events, his presence underscores the faithful remnant committed to God's house.
